questions.question: What should you do if you experience a tyre blowout while driving?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow down

questions.explanation: Braking immediately during a blowout can make you lose control, and you should never accelerate. Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.

questions.question: What is the rule for using a roundabout?

options.text: Give way to traffic from your left
Give way to traffic from your right

questions.explanation: At a roundabout traffic approaches from the right, so you must give way to traffic from your right.

questions.question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign with a black arrow indicate?
questions.explanation: The video gives 'sharp bend ahead'. Note: the NaTIS manual has no yellow diamond-shaped warning sign. South African warning signs are triangles with a red border (yellow-background versions are temporary signs), and the sharp curve sign is W204/W205.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §4.2 Direction of movement signs (p.25)

questions.question: What must you do before changing lanes on a busy road?

options.text: Check mirrors, blind spots, and use indicators
Change lanes quickly without slowing down

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots for vehicles in that lane, and use your indicator to tell other road users which lane you intend to move into.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: At a flashing red traffic light you must stop, and proceed only when it is safe to do so (as at a stop sign).

questions.question: What should you do if an animal crosses the road in front of you?

options.text: Speed up to scare it away
Slow down or stop if necessary

questions.explanation: If an animal crosses the road in front of you, slow down or stop if necessary.

questions.question: When are you allowed to drive in the emergency lane?
questions.explanation: It is called an emergency lane for a reason: you may only use it in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the maximum legal speed limit on South African national roads outside urban areas?
questions.explanation: The video gives 120 km/h. Note: in the NaTIS manual the general limit is 120 km/h on a freeway, but 100 km/h on any other public road outside an urban area. So the answer depends on whether the national road is a freeway.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.27 Speed limits (p.24)

questions.question: How should you react if you see a school zone sign?
questions.explanation: If you see a school zone sign you must slow down, as children may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a white bar in the middle mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a white horizontal bar in the middle is the no entry sign.

questions.question: What must you do at a stop sign?

options.text: Slow down and proceed if the road is clear
Stop completely and only proceed when it is safe

questions.explanation: At a stop sign you must come to a complete stop, even if there are no other cars, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign with a white arrow indicate?

options.text: A direction that must be followed

questions.explanation: A blue circular sign with a white arrow is a command sign: you must go in the direction shown.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a freeway?
questions.explanation: You may not stop, reverse or make a U-turn on a freeway. Continue to the next exit and take that one.

questions.question: When driving at night, when should you switch to low-beam headlights?
questions.explanation: Dip your headlights when approaching another vehicle so that you do not blind its driver.

questions.question: What does a triangular road sign with a red border indicate?
questions.explanation: Triangular signs with a red border are warning signs: they warn of hazards ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid double yellow line in the center of the road mean?
questions.explanation: The video says a solid double line in the centre means no overtaking. Note: in South Africa, no-overtaking lines in the centre of the road are white (RM1); yellow lines mark the road edge.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §7.1 Regulatory markings, No overtaking lines RM1 (p.48)

questions.question: What is the purpose of a traffic circle (roundabout)?

options.text: To allow faster vehicles to pass
To allow a smooth flow of traffic without stopping

questions.explanation: A traffic circle allows a smooth flow of traffic without stopping.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to skid on a wet road?

options.text: Turn in the direction of the skid
Turn in the opposite direction of the skid

questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, steer in the direction of the skid. Do not slam on the brakes.

questions.question: When are you allowed to use your hazard lights while driving?

options.text: When driving in heavy rain or fog
Only when stopped or stationary to indicate an emergency

questions.explanation: Hazard lights are only used when you are stopped or stationary, to indicate an emergency.

questions.question: What does a red triangle with a black exclamation mark inside indicate?

options.text: Warning of a general hazard ahead

questions.explanation: A red triangle with a black exclamation mark warns of a general hazard ahead.
